title: clean: cargo's CACHEDIR.TAG test takes other tools' caches, the elixir and swift arms run cargo's search and print its note, --dry-run writes a marker, and the shared-tree warning fires on ordinary layouts
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 by 0115's page agent for `clean`, and driven again by cc at 4c9d5a7 in fixtures of cc's own (lib/ there is byte-identical to HEAD's). Six points, all in lib/cmd/clean but the last. One body, _clean_run, serves the three arms.

1. `clean rust` TAKES ANY DIRECTORY HOLDING A CACHEDIR.TAG, WHICHEVER TOOL WROTE IT. _clean_roots searches for the file (lib/cmd/clean:237-241) and _clean_has_markers accepts it as a cargo marker (:311). CACHEDIR.TAG is a cross-tool convention: pytest, mypy and others write the same signature line. DRIVEN: beside a Cargo.toml, `.pytest_cache/` carrying pytest's own tag was listed with target/ as "rust: 2 target tree(s)", and `clean rust --force` removed both. The file says cargo's markers are "written by the tool itself" (:303). A tag names its writer on its second line: cargo's reads "# This file is a cache directory tag created by cargo." (read off real cargo trees on this machine, Utilz's and Laksa's target/). .rustc_info.json and debug/.fingerprint are cargo's alone.

2. THE ELIXIR AND SWIFT ARMS RUN CARGO'S MARKER SEARCH. _clean_roots unions the CACHEDIR.TAG and .rustc_info.json search into every arm's candidates (:237-241), and for `_build` and `.build` _clean_has_markers then classifies each such hit as not-build (:316-318). DRIVEN: in a project holding target/, _build/ and .build/, both `clean elixir --dry-run` and `clean swift --dry-run` printed "1 director(y|ies) named like a build tree with no build markers -- not touched" and listed target/ as ignored. The count line prints "director(y|ies)" literally (:473).

3. THE ELIXIR AND SWIFT ARMS PRINT CARGO'S NOTE. "This takes release/ as well as debug/ -- that is what makes it a release verb rather than a cache sweep" (:545-546) sits in the shared body. DRIVEN under both arms.

4. `--dry-run` WRITES INTO THE PROJECT. _clean_mark places .metadata_never_index in each skipped tree (:462), before the dry-run stop (:552), whose comment says the preview has "PRINTED EVERYTHING AND CHANGED NOTHING" (:548). DRIVEN: a dry run over a cargo tree with no Cargo.toml beside it printed "marked .../sub/target/.metadata_never_index", and that file was the one thing the run created outside tmp/.

5. THE PER-NODE TEST FIRES ON ORDINARY LAYOUTS. _clean_peer_dirs lists every lower-case subdirectory except debug, release, package, doc and tmp as another session's cache (:333-345), and any hit prints "THIS TREE IS SHARED ... Announce it first." (:539-543). DRIVEN, each enough on its own: Mix's _build/dev and _build/test; SwiftPM's .build/arm64-apple-macosx, .build/checkouts and .build/repositories; cargo's target/aarch64-apple-darwin and target/criterion; and pytest's .pytest_cache/v, through point 1. A warning that fires on every Elixir project teaches its readers to skip the one case it exists for: sessions sharing a target/ through CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/<node>.

6. THE CATALOGUE OVERCLAIMS FOR `elixir`. clean.elixir's summary, which help prints, says "deps/ is left alone" (lib/builtins:129). A `_build` inside deps/<dep>/, beside that dependency's mix.exs, is removed. DRIVEN: `clean elixir --force` removed deps/jason/_build and kept deps/jason/lib/jason.ex. The reason for sparing deps/ (lib/cmd/clean:587-589: a download, not a build product) still holds. The words promise more than the arm does.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO:
- Keep cargo's markers to cargo. A CACHEDIR.TAG counts only when it names cargo as its writer, or it stops being a marker and .rustc_info.json and .fingerprint carry the test. The build says which, and why.
- Search for markers in the rust arm only, print the release/ note only there, and fix the plural.
- A dry run marks nothing. It may say what a real run would mark.
- The per-node test lists a subdirectory only when that subdirectory is itself a cargo build tree. A nested CARGO_TARGET_DIR is one; a Mix env, a SwiftPM triple, a cargo target-triple directory and criterion's reports are not. Which marker separates a nested target dir from a target-triple dir is to be read off a real cargo tree before the test is written, not assumed. One real case is on this machine: Intent's native/rust/target holds `staging`, a nested target dir carrying CACHEDIR.TAG and .rustc_info.json, beside `test-home`, which carries neither. By the code (:333-345) both would be listed as per-node caches today. That is inferred, not driven: a dry run there would write into Intent's tree (point 4).
- The summary says what the arm does: the sources under deps/ stay.

PAGES. 0115's clean.md states points 1 and 5 as the rules they are today: its line on what a rust candidate is, and its paragraph on the shared-tree warning. The fix edits both in the same change. It ships in 0.1.8 under hv's ruling. cc's.

7. THE SCAN IS BLIND TO WHAT find CANNOT READ, AND SAYS NOTHING. Added at vc's request on 2026-09-23. _clean_roots runs find with its errors sent to /dev/null (lib/cmd/clean:231-245, eg :236), and its caller reads it through a process substitution (:297), so find's status is lost as well. A tree under a directory find cannot read is never enumerated, and the run cannot know it. DRIVEN: with one directory unreadable (chmod 000), `clean rust --dry-run` reported "1 target tree(s)", exit 0, with no word about the directory, where the readable control found 2. The file's own comment calls a tree that appears in no output at all the worse direction (:223).

THE FIX FOR POINT 7 (vc, 2026-09-23). Remove what was found, since acting on what the scan saw is the safe direction. Name each path find could not read, say the scan was partial, and exit 1. A partial clean is not a clean, and a zero lets `clean && build` build on trees nobody looked at: 0056's rule, where a scan that could not read everything exits non-zero. It is the same answer 0127 gives for the vendored find, with one difference: install and upgrade refuse before acting on a partial list, because vendoring or retiring from half a list is not safe, while clean acts on what it saw first. In both, find's error stays on stderr and no success is claimed.

## Resolution

Fixed at 81a8274, one commit with 0137 and 0141. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. Each of the seven points, as the issue states them: cargo's markers are cargo's, its tag matched as a whole line; only the rust arm searches for them and prints the release/ note; a dry run marks nothing; a per-node directory is one holding .rustc_info.json, and a target/ holding only such directories is a tree; the elixir summary says what the arm does; and a scan that cannot read everything says so and exits 1, naming what it could not read. The reviews added: a walk that is one find, pruning at every candidate found by name and walking a crate named like the tree, starting with -H and -mindepth 1, and asking /bin/sh its questions, so nothing it runs is found through PATH; a directory it can read but not search named, and the scan partial; one helper for the markers that need no read; a candidate any option cannot read listed as unread, and so a cargo candidate with an unsearchable subdirectory; a candidate or tag that vanishes mid-scan making nothing partial; --refuse-partial, passed by fullcycle's clean phase, which refuses a partial scan before anything is removed or marked; one pure verdict, checked where it is made, and a confirm step that goes on only for ask or remove; and a PATH guard that reads each path as the kernel does -- a physical cd, a relative path spelled from ./, a leading // folded, a relative answer read -- and looks for binaries in every debug/ and release/ within two levels of a tree, since this change made per-node-only targets removable and a link into target/cc/debug went dark unsaid. clean.md and fullcycle.md say each of these.
- NOT CHANGED, ON THE RECORD. A second copy of the physical-directory step stays in release_scratch (lib/release.steps:195 and :199). Its inputs are absolute, and none of the cases fixed here reaches it; hoisting the helper into lib/helpers for both is a refactor, carried on vc's parked list for the line rather than filed.
- REVIEWS. critic-shell's six passes, each on the delta since the last; the sixth found 0 critical, 1 warning, 4 recommendations and 5 style points, all built or answered, and the commit message names each point with the pass that raised it. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-24, approved on the brief, the interdiff and the evidence.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Each pass's arms were red, on the tree that pass reviewed, for the defect each names, and those green by construction are held by mutants. 75 mutants, 75 killed, each against the arm aimed at it after a baseline of those arms with none red; three survived a first run and each was answered -- an arm gone blind given a half (Z38), the confirm step's default restored (M9), and one equivalent retired with its reason (Z39). The commit message lists them.
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit on main b0b32c2 with exactly this change applied: 1749 of 1749 ok, 0 not ok, its 5 skips the suite's declared ones. The last round's arms, with three earlier ones on the walk it touched, ran under bash 5.0, 5.1 and 5.2 and under GNU find: 10 of 10 under each.
